title: Weekly Engineering Standup
description: Short sync across backend, frontend, QA and support.
transcript: Morning. Let's keep this to fifteen minutes. James, start us off.
Morning. Yesterday was all incident follow-up — writing the postmortem, mostly.
Today I'm finishing that and then I'm back on the mobile auth flow from Monday.
Good. That's the plan Sarah and I agreed yesterday.
I shipped the transcript virtualisation change on Friday. It's been in production over the weekend with no errors.
Scroll performance on the long meetings is dramatically better. We were rendering twelve hundred nodes, now it's about forty.
I can confirm that. I was testing on the design review recording and it used to lock up my laptop.
Yeah, that one was the worst case.
One thing — the jump-to-current button occasionally flickers when you scroll fast. It's cosmetic but it looks broken.
I know what's causing it. The programmatic scroll is triggering the user-scrolled handler.
Half a day. I'll pick it up today.
Do it. Cosmetic bugs in the main view cost us more than they look like they should.
Two things. First, I've finished the regression pass on the export feature and there's one real bug.
PDF export breaks if the meeting title contains a forward slash. It's trying to use the title as a filename.
It is. It's been there since the feature shipped, I think — nobody had a slash in a title until this week.
That's a filename sanitisation thing. I can fix that in twenty minutes.
It's a bit worse than it looks — it's not just slashes. Dot-dot works too.
That's a path traversal, not a cosmetic bug.
That's why I flagged it as the first thing.
Right. James, drop the postmortem and do that first.
Nina, what was the second thing?
Much smaller. The date filter on the meetings list is off by one at the end of the range.
If you filter to a range ending today, meetings from today don't appear.
That's the classic inclusive-end bug. The query is using less-than rather than less-than-or-equal on the date.
That's what it looks like from the outside.
Yes — two tickets last week. Both users assumed the filter was broken and gave up.
Then it's worth fixing. David, can you take it?
Ticket volume is down about fifteen percent week on week, which is mostly the incident traffic clearing.
The thing I want to raise is that we're getting repeat questions about where recordings are stored.
Six tickets in two weeks, all essentially the same question. There's nothing in the docs that answers it clearly.
That's a documentation gap, not a support gap.
That's my read too. I can draft something if someone will check it for accuracy.
James, can you review it when Yuki has a draft?
Quick one — are we still doing the Friday demo? It's been cancelled twice.
Yes, and that's on me. Let's actually do it this week.
I'd like to show the export regression suite if there's time.
There will be. Right — that's us. Thanks everyone.

summary.overview: Transcript virtualisation shipped Friday and is stable in production, cutting rendered nodes from roughly twelve hundred to forty. Nina found a path-traversal bug in PDF export where the meeting title is used unsanitised as a filename, which was escalated to top priority ahead of the incident postmortem. A separate off-by-one in the meetings date filter excludes same-day meetings from an inclusive range and has generated two support tickets. Yuki raised a documentation gap around recording storage that has produced six near-identical tickets in two weeks.
summary.gist: Virtualisation shipped clean; export filename bug is a path traversal and jumps the queue.

outline.title: Yuki — support volume and docs gap

bullets: Live since Friday, no errors over the weekend.
Rendered DOM nodes down from ~1,200 to ~40 on long meetings.
Remaining issue: jump-to-current flickers because programmatic scroll triggers the user-scroll handler.
PDF export uses the meeting title as a filename without sanitisation.
Forward slashes break it; `..` sequences make it a path traversal rather than a cosmetic bug.
Present in production since the feature shipped; reprioritised above the postmortem.
A range ending today excludes meetings from today — inclusive-end handled as `<` rather than `<=`.
Two support tickets; both users concluded the filter was broken.

notes.chapter: Yuki — support volume and docs gap
bullets: Ticket volume down ~15% week on week as incident traffic clears.
Six tickets in two weeks asking where recordings are stored — nothing in the docs answers it.

action_items.text: Fix filename sanitisation in PDF export — path traversal via meeting title
Fix the jump-to-current flicker caused by programmatic scroll
Fix the inclusive-end off-by-one in the meetings date filter
Draft documentation on where recordings are stored
Review Yuki's storage documentation for technical accuracy
